questions.q: What does SOSL stand for, and what is it for?
options: Salesforce Org Security Language: managing permissions
Salesforce Object Search Language: searching for text across multiple objects
Salesforce Object Sorting Language: sorting query results
Structured Object Sync Language: syncing data between orgs
questions.explain: SOSL is the Salesforce Object Search Language, a text search that can span many objects in one request.

questions.q: Which SOSL statement finds Accounts, Contacts and Leads mentioning Acme in any searchable field?
options: SEARCH 'Acme' IN Account, Contact, Lead
SELECT * FROM Account, Contact, Lead WHERE Name = 'Acme'
FIND {Acme} IN ALL FIELDS RETURNING Account, Contact, Lead
FIND Acme FROM Account, Contact, Lead
questions.explain: SOSL uses FIND with the term in braces, an IN scope, and RETURNING to list the objects. It has no FROM or WHERE.

questions.q: What does the IN clause of a SOSL statement control?
options: Which kinds of fields are searched, such as ALL FIELDS, NAME FIELDS, or EMAIL FIELDS
How many records are returned
Which user's records are visible
Which objects are returned
questions.explain: IN sets the search scope. RETURNING chooses the objects, and LIMIT caps the results.

questions.q: What do the wildcards * and ? do in a SOSL search term?
options: SOSL does not support wildcards
* matches any number of characters; ? matches exactly one
Both match any number of characters
* matches exactly one character; ? matches any number
questions.explain: In SOSL, * matches zero or more characters and ? matches exactly one.

questions.q: Which is true of SOSL search results?
options: Newly created records are always searchable instantly
They come from text fields only and return up to 2,000 records in total
They always return every matching record with no cap
They can match numeric and date fields directly
questions.explain: SOSL searches text-type fields, caps results at 2,000 records, and uses a search index that can lag briefly behind new or edited records.
